title: Extraction Methods
text: Start detect_tables() see engines find automatically:
code: library(macrox)  sess <- mx_session("report.pdf") sess |> detect_tables(pages = 1:20)

title: Extraction Methods
text: Uses pdftools::pdf_data() word-level bounding boxes. Java required. Works PDF selectable text. Best : PDFs charts sharing page tables, missing grid lines, numbers run together without whitespace. locate_area() opens interactive click-drag selector rendered page image. returned numeric vector c(top, left, bottom, right) can hardcoded macro.
code: area <- sess |> locate_area(page = 8) sess |> select_table("monthly", page = 8, area = area, method = "bbox")

title: Extraction Methods
text: Two parameters control words grouped rows columns:
code: sess |> select_table("financials", page = 12, method = "bbox",   area    = c(top = 80, left = 30, bottom = 500, right = 750),   col_gap = 20,   # widen if two columns merge into one   row_tol = 3)    # increase if words on the same row are misaligned

title: Extraction Methods
text: Government PDFs often two- three-row header structures. Use header_rows flatten :
code: # Two-row header: group label in row 1, sub-labels in row 2 sess |> select_table("breed_sire", page = 16, area = area,   method = "bbox", header_rows = 2) # Column names become e.g. "Group_A.Jan", "Group_A.Feb", "Group_B.Sub1"

title: Extraction Methods
text: Wrappers around tabulapdf. Require Java tabulapdf package (listed Suggests). Java available, macrox falls back bbox warning.
code: sess |> select_table("calf_monthly", page = 8, method = "lattice") sess |> select_table("roster",       page = 9, method = "stream")  # By table index when multiple tables are on the same page sess |> select_table("sire_beef",  page = 15, table_index = 1) sess |> select_table("sire_dairy", page = 15, table_index = 2)

title: Extraction Methods

title: Extraction Methods
text: Docling caches converted pages memory, extracting multiple tables page fast. Call close_docling() session complete free memory.
code: # Scan for tables using Docling's ML detection sess |> detect_tables(pages = 1:20, method = "docling")  # Extract a specific table (by table_index on that page) sess |> select_table_docling("financials", page = 10, table_index = 1)  # Release the in-memory document cache when done close_docling()

title: Extraction Methods
text: handle scanned PDFs. Choose Docling : need offline / air-gapped operation process many pages (Docling faster LLM scale) Layout complex headers single-row Choose LLM : Headers multi-level spanning schema matters table occupies irregular bounding box already LLM provider set

title: Extraction Methods
text: Instead specifying page number, point macrox caption finds table : Useful page numbers shift report editions. macrox scans pdf_text() output page, scores target caption, selects best match within max_dist.
code: sess |> select_table("mart_breed",   label_match  = "Mart Movements by Breed",   fuzzy_method = "jw",     # Jaro-Winkler (default), also "lv", "dl", "cosine"   max_dist     = 0.2)      # maximum acceptable distance (0 = exact, 1 = anything)

title: Extraction Methods
text: table continues across several consecutive pages, stack_pages() extracts page row-binds results. default, header_match = TRUE — rows pages 2+ look like header row (matching column names) discarded automatically. Turn table repeated header: multi-page tables complex irregular headers, use LLM method — see LLM Integration vignette.
code: sess |> stack_pages("breed_all", pages = 10:14,   area   = c(top = 80, left = 30, bottom = 700, right = 550),   method = "bbox") sess |> stack_pages("breed_all", pages = 10:14,   method       = "bbox",   header_match = FALSE)

title: LLM Integration
text: Add lines .Rprofile never specify provider model call: Supported providers: "anthropic", "openai", "google_gemini", "openrouter", "groq", "ollama", "openai_compatible", provider ellmer exports chat_<provider>() constructor.
code: options(   macrox.llm.provider = "anthropic",   macrox.llm.model    = "claude-opus-4-8" )

title: LLM Integration
text: Call mx_configure_llm() per session avoid repeating provider/model every extraction call: configured, subsequent select_table_llm() select_item() calls session use provider without arguments.
code: library(macrox)  sess <- mx_session("report.pdf")  # Option 1: provider + model (uses global options as defaults) sess |> mx_configure_llm(provider = "anthropic", model = "claude-opus-4-8")  # Option 2: pass a fully-configured ellmer Chat object for maximum control chat <- ellmer::chat_anthropic(   model  = "claude-opus-4-8",   system = "Extract data exactly as shown in the document." ) sess |> mx_configure_llm(chat = chat)

title: LLM Integration
text: auto-detected columns need adjusting, use update_llm_schema() revise without re-browsing:
code: # After initial extraction, refine column names and types sess |> update_llm_schema("livestock",   schema = c(     Breed    = "character",     Bulls    = "integer",     Cows     = "integer",     Heifers  = "integer",     Total    = "integer"   ) )  # Revise the prompt too sess |> update_llm_schema("livestock",   schema = c(Breed = "character", Total = "integer"),   prompt = "Only extract the Breed and Total columns." )

title: LLM Integration
text: select_item() extracts single value sits outside table — publication date, invoice number, report title. Results accumulate sess$items alongside sess$tables. Supported cast values: "character" (default), "numeric", "integer", "date:<strptime_format>".
code: # Extract from all-pages text (no page rendering needed) sess |> select_item("pub_date",   prompt = "Publication or report date in the header or footer." )  # Cast the result directly sess |> select_item("pub_date",   prompt = "Publication date.",   cast   = "date:%d/%m/%Y" )  # Extract from a specific page image for better accuracy sess |> select_item("issue_number",   prompt = "Issue or reference number shown on the cover page.",   page   = 1L )  # View all extracted items sess |> show_items()

title: LLM Integration
code: sess |> update_item("pub_date",   prompt = "Date shown at the top of page 1 in DD/MM/YYYY format.",   cast   = "date:%d/%m/%Y" )

title: LLM Integration
code: sess |> select_item("invoice_number",   prompt  = "Invoice ID or reference number",   backend = "gliner" )  sess |> select_item("total_amount",   prompt  = "Grand total amount payable",   page    = 1L,   cast    = "numeric",   backend = "gliner" )  # Retrieve all occurrences (e.g. all dates mentioned) sess |> select_item("dates_mentioned",   prompt      = "Date or dates mentioned in the document",   backend     = "gliner",   all_matches = TRUE )

title: LLM Integration
text: GLiNER runs one inference pass fields — much faster calling select_item() loop:
code: sess |> select_items_batch(   items = c(     invoice_number = "Invoice ID or reference number",     vendor_name    = "Supplier or vendor name",     total_amount   = "Grand total amount payable",     due_date       = "Payment due date"   ),   cast = c(     total_amount = "numeric",     due_date     = "date:%d/%m/%Y"   ) )

title: LLM Integration
text: select_struct() uses GLiNER2’s extract_json pull multiple records defined schema — useful line-item tables GLiNER handles better tabulapdf: resulting table value columns plus <field>_conf columns per-field GLiNER confidence scores. Use min_confidence filter uncertain extractions.
code: sess |> select_struct("line_items",   fields = c(     description = "Item description or product name",     qty         = "Quantity ordered",     unit_price  = "Unit price per item",     total       = "Line total amount"   ),   list_fields  = character(0),             # none in this case   page         = 2L,   gliner_model = "fastino/gliner2-base-v1" # or "-large-v1" for better accuracy )  # Convert raw records to a data frame (includes per-field confidence scores) sess |> struct_to_df("line_items",   min_confidence = 0.6   # drop low-confidence records; NULL keeps all )  # Now available as sess$tables[["line_items"]] for downstream steps

title: LLM Integration
text: table spans several pages irregular multi-level header, combine stack_pages() method = "llm": stack_pages() extracts page independently row-binds results. header_match = TRUE default discards repeated header rows pages 2+.
code: sess |> stack_pages("breed_all",   pages  = 10:14,   method = "llm",   schema = c(     Breed  = "character",     Month  = "character",     Male   = "integer",     Female = "integer"   ) )

title: Macros & Testing
text: Every step run session silently recorded. Call save_macro() done: Next year — one call replays every step:
code: library(macrox)  sess <- mx_session("report_2024.pdf")  sess |> select_table("monthly", page = 8, method = "bbox") sess |> rename_columns("monthly", c(Month = "month", Total = "total")) sess |> cast_types("monthly", c(total = "integer")) sess |> filter_rows("monthly", exclude_where = "month == 'Total'")  sess |> save_macro("my_report") # Writes my_report.yml to the working directory tables <- mx_replay("report_2025.pdf", macro = "my_report")  tables$monthly   # clean data frame, ready to use

title: Getting Started with macrox
text: Sends rendered page image large language model. Best multi-level spanning headers, scanned PDFs, layout positional extraction fails. Requires ellmer package provider API key .Renviron. Using chat = — pass ellmer chat object full control model parameters, system prompts, provider configuration: Using provider = — shorthand defaults fine. provider can name ellmer chat constructor without chat_ prefix — e.g. "anthropic", "openai", "google_gemini", "openrouter", "groq", "mistral", "deepseek", "ollama", "openai_compatible".
